title: boost database_query read-only guard lets side-effecting SELECTs through
description: The MCP tool database_query accepts any single statement that starts with SELECT, WITH, EXPLAIN or VALUES and contains no write keyword. Statements such as SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE, SELECT LOAD_FILE(...), SELECT pg_read_file(...), SELECT pg_terminate_backend(...), SELECT pg_sleep(600) and SELECT SLEEP(600) pass the filter, and a read-only transaction does not stop file access, backend control or sleeps.
root_cause: The guard is a denylist of write keywords only; it does not cover INTO or functions with server-side effects.
intended_behavior: database_query runs one read-only statement and refuses anything that writes data, reads or writes server files, or controls other sessions.

trace.description: An MCP client (an AI agent) supplies the query string.
The filter checks only readOnlyStart and writeKeyword, neither of which matches INTO or the listed functions.
The statement is executed on the application database connection.

evidence.description: TestSecurity_A05_BoostQueryRefusesSideEffectingSelects: before the fix every listed query reached the database (the SQLite test database rejected them only because the functions do not exist there).
Phase 5 re-check: the first pattern required a parenthesis right after the name, so pg_sleep/**/(600) passed; the name alone is matched now (case added to the same test).

conditions.description: The developer runs the boost MCP server against a database whose account has the privilege (FILE, pg_read_server_files, pg_signal_backend) for the function.
An AI agent connected to the MCP server is steered (prompt injection) to issue the query.

execution.attacker_perspective: An agent or prompt-injected content calling the database_query tool.
instructions: Run the boost MCP server against a local test database.
Observe that the guard does not return the read-only error; the statement reaches the database.
execution.observed_result: The guard accepted the statements and the database was asked to run them (the SQLite fixture failed with a SQL error instead of the read-only refusal).

remediation.strategy: Add INTO to the write keywords and refuse calls to file, backend-control, sleep and extension functions.

likelihood.reason: Development-only local tool, needs a privileged database account and an agent steered to the call.

impact.reason: Server file read or write and session termination on a developer database, bounded by database privileges.

confidence.reason: The guard bypass is reproduced locally; the effect depends on database privileges that were not exercised against MySQL or PostgreSQL.
